newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIAN TITLE RACE GOES TO PLAY-OFF.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIAN TITLE RACE GOES TO PLAY-OFF.

text.p: Spartak Moscow came from behind to win 2-1 in St Petersburg on Sunday and force a play-off for the Russian league title with Alania Vladikavkaz, who finished level on points after winning at home.

Yegor Titov's 30-metre winner for Spartak with 17 minutes to play capped a battling comeback by the Moscow side against a determined Zenit St Petersburg, whose disappointed fans showered bottles and cans on the referee after the game.

The date and venue for the play-off have yet to be set. It is the first time the five-year-old Russian championship has gone to a decider. If the two sides are still deadlocked after extra time, the title could be settled by a penalty shoot-out.
Spartak, champions three times running from 1992 to 1994, began the day level with title-holders Vladikavkaz from the Caucasus region of North Ossetia, close to rebel Chechnya.
Alania had much the easier task of the two and comfortably saw off Lokomotiv Nizhny Novgorod 3-1 at home.
Zenit, promoted this season and eager for a win to finish in the top eight and clinch a cash bonus from the city council, shocked Spartak with a goal in three minutes from Igor Danilov.
From then on the pace never let up.
Zenit keeper Roman Berezovsky blundered in the 30th minute, fumbling a crafty, curling Andrei Tikhonov free-kick into the net.

Titov's thumping drive in the 73rd minute also found Berezovsky wanting but Spartak, hampered by the absence of captain and playmaker Ilya Tsymbalar, were unable to sit back on their lead right up to the whistle.

Zenit fans felt hard done by at being denied a late penalty and the referee had to be escorted from the field by police under a hail of missiles -- the latest in a series of crowd disturbances to blight the Russian league this season.

Rotor Volgograd, who led for much of the second half of the season but trailed by two points on Sunday morning, beat stragglers Uralmash Yekaterinburg 2-1 at home. The win came too late to keep Rotor in the running.

Coupled with an extraordinary 5-4 away win at Rostov by fourth-from-bottom KamAZ Naberezhniye Chelny, that result also consigned Uralmash to relegation along with Tekstilshchik Kamyshin and Lada Togliatti.
League officials said last week that the Alania-Spartak play-off was likely to take place in the next few days.
The clubs will have to agree on a neutral ground.

Vladikavkaz might agree to play in Moscow, where they can count on support from thousands of Ossetians living in the capital. Few Russian fans go to away games, so playing in another city would rob the decider of much atmosphere.

Key players from both sides are likely to be in the Russian squad which travels to Luxembourg for next Sunday's World Cup group five qualifier, so league officials may press for the play-off to go ahead in the first half of the week.
